summary: GELF/syslog live-forwarding: tenant-aware pseudonymization, schema evolution plan, and verifiable export proof
description:
Issue summary: Customer requests a near-real-time GELF (Graylog) / syslog-compatible audit feed that preserves event ordering and tenant isolation while applying field-level pseudonymization. They also require a short 'schema evolution plan' describing how new audit fields (e.g., model_id, prompt_hash, response_digest, tokens_cost) will be surfaced to their SIEM without breaking ingestion, and a verifiable evidence bundle showing redaction/pseudonymization applied to a 24-hour live sample.

Impact: Veridian uses the feed for transaction monitoring and internal compliance alerts. Without a usable GELF/syslog export they cannot onboard Redwood audit events into their on-prem SIEM, which blocks a scheduled audit window.

Environment: Production tenants, us-east region (customer-dedicated VPC peering). Customer runs Graylog 4.x and expects GELF over TLS + syslog framing from our forwarder.

Request details:
- Provide a live-forwarding configuration (rsyslog/Filebeat snippet and Redwood end-point settings) that preserves chronological ordering and supplies a resume token for continuity after disconnects.
- Implement or document tenant-scoped pseudonymization for PII-like fields (user_id, prompt_text, user_email) with a reversible mapping for legalhold (customer-managed keywrap) or an irreversible salted hash option.
- Produce a concise schema-evolution plan (CSV mapping + example transformations) for the SIEM team so new fields are opt-in and backward-compatible.
- Deliver a 24-hour evidence bundle: 4 sample gzipped GELF files (each ~1-hour contiguous windows) with redaction applied, a per-file checksum, and a signed manifest that proves the files were produced by Redwood during the requested window. Customer asked that the per-event HMAC use an epoch-based rotating KEK and include an event nonce so they can validate sequence integrity on ingestion.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer configured a custom forwarder in Console > Audit Exports set to 'GELF over TLS' pointing at their Graylog collector on tcp:12201 with TLS verifying Redwood certificate.
Started a small test job that generates user-scoped audit events (login, prompt_send, model_call) for tenant: veridian-prod.
Observed initial TCP connect succeed from Redwood to their collector, then periodic TLS handshake failures after roughly 30 minutes.
During failures some events reappeared out-of-order in Graylog, and the customer saw duplicate events with missing tenant header once a reconnection occurred.
Customer attempted to enable per-event HMAC on their side and reported inability to reconcile sequence numbers because the HMAC envelope did not include the resume token in the payload.
logs: [2026-03-13T10:34:58Z] forwarder: tls: handshake error: remote error: tls: bad certificate (peer=graylog-collector)
[2026-03-13T10:35:08Z] forwarder: resend batch id=2917 count=48 (tenant header missing on 3 events)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: TLS certificate chain mismatch due to SNI mismatch when connecting to Graylog behind a load balancer. Explains periodic handshake failures.

Second hypothesis: When reconnect occurs our batching window resends partial batches without reattaching tenant metadata header for in-flight items; edge case in our forwarder buffer flush logic causes duplicate events without tenant envelope.

Observed that the current HMAC envelope in production signs only the event.body; it does not include the resume_token or batch_id. Customer validation requires HMAC over (event.body || resume_token || epoch_nonce).

Checked Console export config: customer had 'compress=true' and 'frame=gelf-framed' enabled which interacts poorly with some Graylog parsers when log messages contain embedded newlines. Recommending JSON compacting and newline escaping for safe GELF payloads.
comments: Ana Rodriguez (Support) 2026-03-13: Acknowledged; requested they provide a small traceroute, openssl s_client log, and a representative sample of a truncated message. Escalated to infra on-call.

Marcus Patel (Engineering) 2026-03-13: Investigating forwarder buffer flush; will reproduce locally with a Graylog container. Asked for their Graylog configuration (input settings) and whether they terminate TLS at LB or collector.

Customer (Veridian SIEM) 2026-03-13: Provided s_client output and noted LB terminates TLS and rewrites SNI to collector.internal.veridian.local. Asked if Redwood can include the original tenant header inside the GELF 'short_message' field to avoid parsing issues.

Marcus Patel (Engineering) 2026-03-14: Confirmed bug in buffer flush logic that strips the 'X-Redwood-Tenant' metadata for retries (fix branch created, PR #4512). Working on adding resume_token into HMAC envelope per customer request.

Ana Rodriguez (Support) 2026-03-14: Proposed workaround: enable 'explicit-tenant-in-payload' toggle in export config (server-side partial rollout) + provide rsyslog/Filebeat example to run on-prem while we ship fix. Customer accepted temporary approach pending signed evidence bundle.
resolution:
Workaround delivered: enabled 'explicit-tenant-in-payload' on the customer's export (opt-in flag) so each GELF message includes a canonical 'tenant_id' and 'resume_token' fields inside the JSON payload. Provided rsyslog and Filebeat snippets adapted to Graylog TLS termination at LB. Engineering merged fix (PR #4512) that preserves tenant header across retries and includes the resume_token in the HMAC envelope.

Evidence bundle: Uploaded 4 gzipped hour-slices to a customer S3 path with per-file sha256 checksums and a signed manifest (manifest signed with Redwood platform key; customer requested separate keywrap for legalhold — provided instructions to enable customer-managed KEK for future bundles).

Follow-up items: 1) Product task to add native 'GELF over TLS (tenant-envelope)' export type with configurable HMAC fields and rotation schedule. 2) Ops playbook to validate SNI behavior for LB-terminated TLS in dedicated VPCs. 3) Documentation update with schema-evolution CSV and Filebeat mapping examples. Ticket moved to Resolved pending customer confirmation of evidence validity.
